title: His Last ODI Was Against Afghanistan. Three Years Later, His Comeback Is Against Them Too.
excerpt: Ishan Kishan returns to India's ODI squad for the first time since the 2023 World Cup, earning a recall through relentless domestic performance after being frozen out by the BCCI.
body:
Ishan Kishan's last One-Day International was on October 11, 2023. India were playing Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi, in the middle of a World Cup campaign that would end with a heartbreaking final loss to Australia. Kishan kept wicket, scored 30, and walked off the field without knowing it would be almost three years before he wore the blue jersey in this format again.

On Saturday, the BCCI announced India's squad for the three-match ODI series against Afghanistan — the first ODI at the HPCA Stadium in Dharamshala on June 13, followed by Lucknow on June 17 and Chennai on June 20. Kishan's name was on the list. Against Afghanistan, again. Cricket's symmetries can be quietly cruel, but this one felt more like a second chance gift-wrapped in coincidence.

## The Fall

The story of Kishan's exile is well known in Indian cricket circles. After the 2023 World Cup, the BCCI expected players not selected for the tour of South Africa to play domestic cricket. Kishan, along with a few others, did not report. The board took a hard line. For most of 2024 and much of 2025, his name was conspicuously absent from every India squad announcement.

It was not a ban. No official statement was ever released. But in the unspoken grammar of Indian cricket's selection politics, the message was clear: play Ranji Trophy, prove your commitment, and only then will we talk.

Kishan, to his credit, eventually did exactly that. He returned to domestic cricket, first for Jharkhand in the Ranji Trophy, then in the Vijay Hazare Trophy and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. His numbers were consistent — a string of fifties, a century against Bengal, and the kind of quiet, unglamorous performances that don't trend on social media but show up in selection meetings.

## The Recall

Chief selector Ajit Agarkar, speaking after the squad announcement, confirmed that Kishan's domestic form had earned him the recall. "Consistent domestic performances have finally helped Kishan make a comeback after a gap of almost three years," Agarkar noted.

Kishan joins an ODI squad led by Shubman Gill, with Shreyas Iyer as vice-captain. The squad is without Virat Kohli, who tore his hamstring during the IPL final and has been ruled out. Yashasvi Jaiswal comes in as Kohli's replacement. Rohit Sharma and Hardik Pandya are both included but subject to fitness clearances — their availability will be confirmed closer to the first match.

The squad also features a potential debutant in Prince Yadav, the tall right-arm pacer from Lucknow Super Giants who impressed in a difficult IPL season for his franchise.

## What It Means for India

Kishan's inclusion is not sentimental. India are building toward the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will be held in Africa, and Gill's side needs to figure out its middle-order and wicketkeeping combinations across multiple formats. KL Rahul is the primary keeper in the ODI squad, but Kishan's left-handed batting at No. 4 or 5 offers a different option — one that worked in the 2023 World Cup.

Afghanistan, meanwhile, will be no pushovers. Rashid Khan returns to the ODI squad after sitting out the Test. Ibrahim Zadran is in the form of his life, having just scored an unbeaten 120 to seal a series win for Afghanistan against Zimbabwe. And Rahmat Shah, who crossed 1,000 Test runs in the Mullanpur match last week, has been batting with a freedom that suggests he has found a new gear.

## The NRI Angle

For the Indian diaspora watching from the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada, Kishan's return is a reminder of something that makes Indian cricket both maddening and irresistible: nobody is ever truly finished. The same system that can freeze a player out for years can thaw overnight. The same selectors who refused to take his calls six months ago now see him as part of the World Cup plan.

The three ODIs will be broadcast on Star Sports in India and streamed on JioHotstar. For fans in North America, Willow TV will carry the matches live. The first ball at Dharamshala is at 1:30 PM IST — that is 4:00 AM Eastern, 1:00 AM Pacific. Set the alarm. Kishan has waited long enough. The least we can do is watch.
